---
title: "Stage 5 – Your own project"
---
The route ends on a project of your own. You ask a question beyond the claim that SCORE selected from the paper, one that the data of the case support: the other half of a hypothesis of the paper, a different estimand, the second claim of the paper, or the claim on later waves of the survey. The [list below](#the-projects) gives the projects that the case supports and where to start. The project follows the rule of the case report, with one addition. Its preregistration is complete before anything in it runs, and it is also fixed with a date that someone else can check, either as the first commit of the repository of the project, pushed to GitHub, or as a registration on OSF Registries. This stage therefore begins with version control, then writes and commits the preregistration, runs the declared analysis and prepares the work for an archive. It takes about six and a quarter hours of work, and is best spread over several sittings.

## 1. Version control

[90 minutes]{.text-muted}

[Open Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html#sec-why){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Work through the module on git and GitHub on the AR4DS site, from [Version control](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html#sec-why) to [GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html#sec-github). The sections teach version control from first principles, then git on your own machine, with staging, committing, the log and the diffs, and the source-control pane of your IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.). They end on GitHub, remotes, the README, and forks, templates and pull requests.

## 2. The preregistration of the project

[75 minutes]{.text-muted}

[Open the preregistration templates](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-prereg-templates){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The section on registrations describes two templates, the AsPredicted form and the template for secondary data. Write the preregistration of your project with one of them, with a data-in-hand statement that says what you have already looked at in the data. Make it the first commit of a new repository and push it to GitHub, or register it on OSF Registries, before you run anything.

## 3. What to track

[50 minutes]{.text-muted}

[Open What to track](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html#sec-repro){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Read [What to track](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html#sec-repro) and [Your own reanalysis](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html#sec-application). The first says what belongs in a repository and what never does, with licensed survey files as the example of what stays out, and the second puts your own reanalysis under version control, one decision per commit. Add your case report to the repository, with the workspace that renders it. The `.gitignore` file of the workspace keeps out its `data_private/` folder, which holds your respondent file.

## 4. Your project

[130 minutes]{.text-muted}

**In the repository of your project.** Run the specification that you declared, and that one first. Report its result as your preregistration said you would, and place it beside the curve of the case where it can be placed. Label anything that you add after seeing the result as exploratory, and commit as you go.

## 5. Depositing the project

[30 minutes]{.text-muted}

[Open Depositing a reanalysis](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-deposit){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The section sets out a route for depositing a reanalysis of your own. The code goes on a forge, each version is archived with a DOI, the data go where their licence allows and nowhere else, and the plan goes on the OSF with the identifiers of the rest. Write the README of your repository by it.

## 6. Publishing (optional)

[As long as you like]{.text-muted}

[Open Quarto projects](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-housing/companion/quarto.html#sec-project){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

Read [Projects](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-housing/companion/quarto.html#sec-project) and [Publishing the document](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-housing/companion/quarto.html#sec-publish) in the module on Quarto of the housing-audit site. Render your case report and the project together as one Quarto project, and publish the rendered output where other people can reach it.

**Shortcuts.** If you already use git and GitHub, skip the first step and read [What to track](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html#sec-repro) for what the licence of the Eurobarometer files keeps out of a repository.

**By the end of the stage** you have a repository whose first commit is the preregistration of your project as you wrote it, which holds the case report and the project, which leaves out every licensed survey file, and which another person can clone and re-render by following its README; and you have the declared analysis of your project run and reported.

## The projects {#the-projects}

Each item names a direction that the data and the pages of the case support. The question, the specification and the rule by which the result is judged are yours to declare.

- **The negative scales.** You can take the other half of the first hypothesis of the paper, a rise in negative framing, on the negative scales. Start from [The negative scales](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd#negative-scales) on the Multiverse page.
- **A different estimand.** You can take the average European in place of the average member state, with the population weight, or the years before the crisis, the crisis years, or the member states without the bailout countries. Start from [The average European](../../companion/weighting.qmd#the-average-european) in the module on weights, and [Heterogeneity and influence](../../companion/multiverse.qmd#sec-heterogeneity) in the multiverse module.
- **The second claim of the paper.** You can take the gap between education groups, on the simulated respondents of the course or on the respondent file that you built in stage 3, which never leaves your machine. Start from [Claim 2](../../companion/individual-level.qmd#sec-claim2) in the module on the individual level, and [the panel by education band](../../companion/data-management.qmd#sec-edu).
- **Later waves.** You can take the claim to later Eurobarometer waves, such as those of 2013 to 2019 on which the SCORE replication tested it, with the data built by you from the files at GESIS by the route of stage 3. The course has no unit on these waves. Start from [the replication](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd#sec-repetition) in the case study, [the GESIS archive](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-gesis) in the module on data sources, and [Building the analysis file](../../companion/data-management.qmd).
